{{Short description|French chemist (1926–2006)}}
{{Expand French|topic=bio|Guy Ourisson|date=November 2013}}
'''Guy Henry Ourisson''' (March 26, 1926 &ndash; November 4, 2006) was a French [[chemist]]. He was a member of the Academy of Sciences where he was vice president and then became the president. Awarded the [[Ernest Guenther Award]] in 1972 and the [[Heinrich Wieland Prize]] in 1985.

==Career==
In 1952 he obtained a PhD from [[Harvard University]]. In 1954 he obtained a [[doctorate]] in physics from the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] under the direction of G. Dupont. At the [[University of Strasbourg]] he was appointed lecturer in 1955, professor in 1958 and professor emeritus in 1995.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Hargittai|first=István|title=Mosaic of a Scientific Life|publisher=Springer, Cham|pages=129–131}}</ref>

He died, aged 80, in [[Strasbourg]].
